title: Utilizing Strategic Pre-training to Reduce Overfitting: Baguan – A Pre-trained Weather Forecasting Model

problem.claim: Weather forecasting faces overfitting because real-world weather data spans only a few decades.

gap.claim: Weather forecasting needs strategies to mitigate overfitting with existing data because it lacks the data abundance available in fields such as computer vision and natural language processing.

contributions.claim: A pre-training strategy is explored in which an appropriately challenging task introduces locality bias to mitigate overfitting and improve weather-forecasting performance.
Baguan is introduced as a data-driven medium-range weather-forecasting model using a self-supervised Siamese Autoencoder for pre-training and fine-tuning across different lead times.
The pre-trained model is applied to subseasonal-to-seasonal modeling and regional forecasting after fine-tuning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Baguan as a novel data-driven model for medium-range weather forecasting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Baguan is reported to outperform traditional methods with more accurate forecasts.
The pre-trained Baguan is reported to provide robust overfitting control and perform well on downstream S2S and regional forecasting tasks after fine-tuning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Weather forecasting is presented as a longstanding challenge.
Modern AI weather models can surpass traditional NWP, but limited historical data leaves overfitting as a critical issue.
The paper investigates challenging pre-training tasks that introduce locality bias to reduce overfitting.
Baguan combines self-supervised Siamese Autoencoder pre-training with lead-time-specific fine-tuning.
The authors report improved forecasting accuracy, overfitting control, and downstream performance in S2S and regional forecasting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, forecast horizons, or quantitative performance differences.
The abstract does not define the pre-training task or the mechanism by which locality bias is introduced.
The abstract does not provide experimental protocols, ablations, or reproducibility details.
